Hi! I'm a pure math student interested in Sobolev inequalities and PDE. I'm interested in contributing to Mathlib in the area of Sobolev inequalities / functional analysis. I've been looking at Mathlib.Analysis.FunctionalSpaces.SobolevInequality and want to extend or build on it (e.g. Poincaré inequality, Sobolev embeddings, or related PDE applications).
I'm still learning Lean 4, any suggestions on what's missing or where to start? Thanks!

Welcome! There is a bit of theory in the works on Sobolev spaces. I don't know about the Poincare inequality, but I have a Sobolev embedding theorem for H^s (based on the Fourier transform, not Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev)

Moritz Doll said:

Welcome! There is a bit of theory in the works on Sobolev spaces. I don't know about the Poincare inequality, but I have a Sobolev embedding theorem for H^s (based on the Fourier transform, not Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev)

Thanks! Moritz,  would that be a good place to start with Poincaré inequality? Or Is there a better way to proceed given what already exists?

My suggestion is to work on sth else right now at this moment as we still don't have Sobolev space in Mathlib right now (I asked the same question and I have seen the same question asked by several different people since last year...).

(I have a lot to do today, so sorry if my message is a bit incoherent) So the development is currently split into two different parts: the classical theory of Wk,pW^{k,p}Wk,p spaces is done by Michael, Filippo and Floris (building on work by Anatole and Luigi who defined classical distributions), whereas I am working on Hs,pH^{s,p}Hs,p (mainly p = 2) using tempered distributions (and a bit of classical distributions for the localization). You probably have the former in mind, and I can't comment on that. In the case of HsH^sHs, I can tell you that I have the Sobolev embedding theorem and localization, nothing super fancy. That code will not get into mathlib anytime soon (partly because of time and partly because it needs cleanup and I am not 100% that the design decisions are right). If you care about Schwartz functions/tempered distributions (and I think everyone should), then I have quite a few tasks that would make good mathlib contributions and are definitively needed at some point (CcI is dense in Schwartz, principal value, (x±iε)−1(x \pm i \varepsilon)^{-1}(x±iε)−1, Gaussian, etc).
If you want to do something with inequalities, then you could of course also look whether there is something, where you don't need the spaces and just prove the inequality on LpL^pLp (i.e., exactly what Heather and Floris did for the GNS inequality) - maybe Morrey's inequality? (you probably don't need the Sobolev space there, just write down the norm with the normal derivative)

Hi Moritz, thanks for the clear direction! I’d love to take on Morrey's inequality first, Is there a specific timeline or urgency for the inequality from your side? I want to make sure I’m not getting in the way of your progress. I'm also very interested in the other tasks you mentioned, but I'd like to finish inequality first since it's related to my final project for my course.
No, I don't have any stakes in that - I would just be happy to see some more activity in PDEs

just note that if you are interested in contributing to mathlib and have less than 5 PRs merged, then the use of LLM tools is forbidden. If you don't care about contributing to mathlib then obviously whatever, but writing the code yourself will teach you a lot (and people here are happy to help out if you run into any issues)
